summary_paragraph: A 65-year-old man with a history of CNS lymphoma and diabetes insipidus was admitted for his 30th cycle of high-dose methotrexate chemotherapy after presenting with a reported seizure and severe hyponatremia (sodium 124). He had been taken into police custody after being served with a restraining order, during which he intentionally mimicked seizure symptoms to gain hospital admission. Evaluation revealed hyponatremia due to overuse of desmopressin and chronic alcohol use, leading to a diagnosis of SIADH. His sodium was corrected with fluid management and standardized desmopressin dosing. He received chemotherapy without complications, and his methotrexate levels cleared appropriately. His seizure medication was adjusted—Keppra was discontinued due to mood effects, and Topamax was initiated. He was counseled on alcohol use and mental health, with recommendations for outpatient psychiatric follow-up. He was discharged home in stable condition with updated medication instructions and follow-up plans.
